column1: # Short-read QC thresholds (python/short_read_qc.py). FROZEN on 17 November 2026 from real data; see docs/THRESHOLD_FREEZE.md for the evidence and the pilot table.
# How they were set: the read-level measures (quality, Q30, read length, adapters, N, duplication, pair synchrony) were measured on the first read pairs of 40 real runs of
# public-v4 (python/qc_pilot.py, docs/validation/short_read_qc_pilot.tsv, one isolate per species, chosen by position in the cohort's balanced order, never by any tool's
# result); read pairs, depth and read length also against the ENA read counts of the 7,129 public-v4 runs that resolved (cohorts/candidates/contributed-refseq-sra/public-v4.precheck.tsv).
# One value was changed by the pilot, before freezing: adapter_fraction has no reject limit (see its row). Do not change a frozen row after tools have been scored: a changed
# file has a different hash (written to every QC row as thresholds_sha), so results made before and after a change are not comparable.
# direction min: the metric must not fall below the limit; max: must not rise above it.
# warn: the sample proceeds, flagged. reject: the sample is excluded from the primary benchmark when SHORT_READ_QC_MODE=enforce.
# A blank reject means there is no rejection limit for that metric. Integrity failures (unreadable, truncated, empty, malformed
# FASTQ, unequal read counts) always reject and are not listed here.

column6: Fewer pairs cannot cover a bacterial genome at useful depth. Of the 7,129 public-v4 runs that resolved, 4 (0.06%) are under the warn limit (median 2.0 million pairs); none of the 7,867 candidates fell under the reject limit.

Uses the genome size given, or 5 Mb when not given (flagged genome_size_assumed). Plasmid recovery needs depth beyond the chromosome's. Of the 7,129 resolved public-v4 runs, 136 (1.9%) are under the warn limit (median 139x); 9 of the 7,867 candidates (0.1%) fell under the reject limit.
Mean Phred of the sampled bases. 40 real runs: minimum 30, median 35, so neither limit fired.
Share of bases at Q30 or better. 40 real runs: minimum 0.72, 5th percentile 0.81, median 0.89; the warn limit flagged 1 of 40 and the reject limit none.

Median over the shorter mate; very short reads assemble poorly. 40 real runs: 100 to 301, median 151; of the 7,129 resolved public-v4 runs 7 (0.1%) are under the warn limit and none of the 7,867 candidates under the reject limit.

Reads carrying an adapter: stage 3 trims them, so an adapter share is a signal, not a reason to discard. 40 real runs: median 0.1%, but 4 above 10% (12%, 21%, 47%, 66%), all with good quality (Q30 0.84 to 1.0), and the old reject limit of 0.50 would have excluded one of them for something trimming removes. The reject limit was therefore removed before freezing; the warn limit stays.
Read with caution: very high depth also duplicates reads. 40 real runs: maximum 0.28, median 0.01; neither limit fired.
Share of N bases. 40 real runs: maximum 0.0028; neither limit fired.
Read names that disagree between R1 and R2 at the same position: the files are out of sync. An integrity check: 40 real runs had none, and any mismatch is a defect, so a warn limit of 0 is right.

Absolute GC difference from the expected organism GC. INERT by default: the pipeline passes no expected GC, so this row never fires. It is frozen as written and is NOT backed by the pilot (one isolate per species gives no within-species spread); supply --expected-gc only if you accept these limits unvalidated.
